Ana (CSM): Quick sync for HarborView private deploy: week1 dry-run is Friday 9am PT. Preflight shows three items: KMS grants blocked by org SCP, CloudTrail -> S3 failing TLS signed PUT through their egress proxy, and audit retention lifecycle not set. Can we triage now?
Hank (Network Eng): Looks like their proxy does TLS termination and re-signing which breaks S3 signature v4. Two immediate paths: 1) add S3 gateway endpoint so traffic stays in AWS and bypasses proxy, or 2) carve an exception in the proxy to allow CONNECT to s3.amazonaws.com. Which is realistic for them?
Ana (CSM): Security policy leans away from exceptions. They prefer endpoint/route approach.
Leila (Security): KMS: their key policy excludes external principals because of org-level restriction. We either ask them to create a grant for our cross-account writer role during the window, or they must add our role to the key policy. Grant is ephemeral and preferred for least-privilege. Also they asked about rotation: they require annual rotation and need to know if we'll break when alias changes.
Tom (Solutions Eng): Grant during cutover is best. CLI to create grant: `aws kms create-grant --key-id <key-id> --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::555444333222:role/redwood-s3-writer --operations Encrypt GenerateDataKey` We'll verify by running `aws kms generate-data-key` from the assumed role. Regarding rotation: if they swap alias to a new key, grants do not follow — they must recreate the grant. Recommend they enable automatic rotation on the existing CMK instead of swapping aliases at rotation time.
Hank (Network Eng): Route action: add gateway endpoint for S3 and update private route tables to point to endpoint. Also confirm the firewall allows the endpoint prefix list. If firewall blocks PLs, we'll need a NAT fallback. Ops estimate: endpoint+routes 30m, firewall approval up to 4h.
Leila (Security): Bucket policy: CloudTrail delivery requires `Principal` for `cloudtrail.amazonaws.com` and the cross-account delivery role. Also ensure `aws:SourceVpce` or IP restrictions don't block the internal CloudTrail service. I'll draft a minimal bucket policy snippet and send.
Ana (CSM): Action owners: KMS grant — Leila; Endpoint + routes — Hank; Bucket policy & retention — HarborView infra (I'll coordinate). Tom will run smoke tests.
Tom (Solutions Eng): Smoke test plan: 1) once grant + bucket policy applied, I'll trigger a test PutObject using the cross-account role and watch CloudTrail for PutObject DataEvent within 5-10m; 2) verify Firehose/Splunk pickup if SIEM role has read perms.
runbook-bot: runbook created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CS-11209 "HarborView week1 dry-run prep"
Leila (Security): On lifecycle/retention: they requested 2 years for audit logs (customer-specific) but compliance changed to 1 year. Confirmed: 1 year -> Glacier then delete at 3 years. I'll update the policy guidance. Also note: if they enforce object encryption via Bucket Key + KMS, make sure bucket encryption settings align with CMK usage.
Hank (Network Eng): If firewall delay is >2h we'll spin up a small ephemeral NAT gateway for the bootstrap host as a fallback. I'll prepare the terraform snippet and hand it to their ops team.
Ana (CSM): Ingrid (HarborView infra) replied in the customer thread: "We can add the endpoint and policy today; compliance will approve the NAT as fallback if needed." She will apply bucket policy at 4pm PT and allow us a 30m assume-role window for grant creation at 5pm.
Tom (Solutions Eng): I'll be on standby at 5pm to run the put test and confirm CloudTrail ingestion. If anything fails, we roll back and use Redwood-managed bucket per rollback playbook.
Ana (CSM): Thanks team — I'll update the calendar and send agenda to the customer. Please add any questions here. :thumbsup:
